purpose: An isolated redesign demonstration, outside the hub navigation.
content: Campaign name, host, February 14, 2027 deadline, eight workshop outcomes and 60-minute duration retained from the reference. Dates remain unannounced. Copy condensed; no invented results or testimonials.

portrait.treatment: Original image resized and compressed as WebP, without retouching. Display crop fills the text-height host frame on desktop; square framing on small screens.

header: Full Community lockup, thin vertical divider and San Francisco, explicitly requested by Luc for the demo. Equal divider gaps of one actual heart height; city type follows the kit’s city/logo ratio, with a 16 px mobile minimum. Opaque #1b1b1b background while scrolling. Header CTA matches navigation at 16 px, with 8 px vertical and 20 px horizontal padding (40 px height).
removed: Repeated calls to action between every section
interactions: Workshop filters and details are functional. Registration is explicitly a local preview, with no requests or persistence. Links to the original initiative and event pages are provided.
toggle: DEMO_OPPORTUNITIES_ENABLED=false removes the build entry and returns 404 in development. Defaults to true. Restart/rebuild after changing it.

organizer.treatment: Original transparent artwork, unchanged, placed beneath the hero actions.

refinements: Date before hero actions at the same size as the introduction; explicit line break after Lovable. Gradient heart at top:28%, left:-25%, width:150%, with rotate(-27deg) scale(1.4), exactly as supplied by Luc, now split into original vector planes around the globe, following Luc’s latest correction; all copy stays above the scene. Practical copy uses 18 px and 16 px, with a 16 px minimum on mobile. White calls to action are text-only with centered labels. Native anchor scrolling is smooth and targets the visible section intro, below the fixed header rather than the section’s outer padding, with reduced motion respected; other interface elements remain static; the later requested globe rotation is a single arrival at San Francisco, followed by a gentle heartbeat and point-wave loop. Workshop heading enlarged to 64 px on desktop with an explicit break before lowercase “to get going.” Right-hand introduction is white, with 64 px before the filters and 32 px after. Host portrait matches the complete text column height on desktop, with a 32 px gap and 32 px corners; it stacks above the text on small screens. Date is white. Hero secondary action inherits the same text size as the primary button. Hero eyebrow restored from the source at Luc’s request: Free credits · Live sessions · Community, in sentence case. Benefits icons are fully opaque white. How it works has 120 px top and bottom padding and its first step starts on the H2 row. Your host has 32 px added above the portrait/text block; its scroll anchor remains on the inner content. Footer credit spans two lines: Made on the internet / by Lovable Brand Team. All main-section H2s now share the same size and leading tokens (64 px maximum, 1.08 leading, 34 px mobile); facing introductions share white text and the same grid. The globe entrance and arrival motion is the later explicit exception to the otherwise static page. The idea headline is condensed to You see a problem. / Build the solution. to keep the enlarged heading on two lines. Step descriptions opposite the H2 are white too. The hero introduction is white, with explicit breaks after Lovable. and before take the first step. Separating dots have 8 px of extra space on each side. The current navigation section is white with aria-current=location and follows scrolling.

globe.treatment: Original Three.js globe starts on the opposite hemisphere and rotates to San Francisco. Its original heart stays anchored to its final San Francisco surface point throughout the entrance. Only its scale and local rotation change, from small and tilted to its final orientation with a slight overshoot, settling at scale 6.4; no translation or depth flight. The dots reveal outward from the heart. Afterwards, a quiet double heartbeat repeats every 4.2 seconds, launching another spherical light wave over the existing dots without dimming the whole map. Live motion pauses outside the hero and in hidden tabs. Reduced motion uses only a final 2160 px still and releases the renderer. Globe entrance retains the 1400 ms fade/scale/blur from bottom-left, with no entrance blur remaining; base transform remains translate(-144px,-80px) scale(1.4), plus a 10° centre tilt. All changes are opt-in for this isolated demo.
globe.bokeh: Bottom-left for this demo only: original focal-blur direction mirrored horizontally from -28° to -152°. Original kit default remains unchanged.
globe.scroll: Reversible scroll progress sinks the globe by up to 160 px between the vector glow planes; both glow planes rotate up to 16° and grow from 1.4 to 1.6 around their bottom-left corner. A static outer transform preserves the approved starting composition. An 85 ms damped response keeps scrolling continuous in both directions. Reduced motion skips this effect.

glow.treatment: Six original vector paths, filter bounds, Gaussian deviations and paint order preserved exactly. Source SVG retained unchanged; generated back/front SVGs put the original globe between the pale pink and vivid pink layers. Original sRGB fill colors are converted to equivalent high-precision OKLCH with original hex fallbacks. Original sRGB Gaussian filter compositing is retained to match Figma; this is layered blur, not a replacement CSS gradient. No raster glow is used by the demo.

validation.comparison: Original Figma SVG vs recombined back/front SVGs, on #1b1b1b at 1024 × 1032

contentReview.method: Compared the original page and the published demo in Chrome.
retained: Nicole Alos and Socratyc / Socratyc AI Studios
All eight original workshop topics and event identifiers, each 60 minutes
Free credits, live sessions and community
Goal of 1,000 projects; all experience levels welcome; public or private submission
Host startup and accelerator experience; independent ambassador-led initiative
omitted: Separate sharing, founder-network and mentor CTAs
demoDifferences: Registration is a local preview, not a live registration flow
San Francisco and the Lovable Brand Team demo credit were explicitly supplied by Luc, not inferred from the source

indexing: Noindex, nofollow in both HTML robots metadata and the X-Robots-Tag response header. Canonical URL is https://lovable-brands.vercel.app/1000-opportunities. Legacy demo paths permanently redirect to the clean URL. No robots.txt disallow: crawlers must be able to read the noindex directive.
